title: Bot protection for forms
description: Stop signup, login and contact-form spam: server-side Cloudflare Turnstile, hCaptcha and reCAPTCHA v2/v3 token checks (hostname, action, score, age, fail-closed), a privacy-friendly signed proof-of-work challenge with single-use replay protection, a honeypot with minimum fill time, one combined guard and a Fetch wrapper that hides which check failed.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, Web Crypto (crypto.subtle, crypto.getRandomValues), AbortSignal.timeout, btoa/atob and the Fetch Request/Response/FormData APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
solveChallenge in pow.ts also runs in browsers and Web Workers; the rest is server-only because it holds keys and the captcha secret.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time; siteverify calls use the fetch you inject.

configuration: Keep the captcha secret, the proof-of-work key and the honeypot key (each at least 32 bytes, different from each other) in your server secret store and pass them in; the module never reads the environment.
Set expectedHostnames to the hosts that render the widget, expectedAction for Turnstile or reCAPTCHA v3, and minScore (default 0.5) for reCAPTCHA v3.
Leave failOpen off unless an outage of the captcha provider must never block signups; with it on, bots pass during every outage.
Create one guard per form with a server-chosen formId; mount createChallengeHandler with the same form ids and wrap each form's POST handler with protect().
Use MemoryReplayStore on a single server only; with several instances implement ReplayStore.consume atomically (Redis SET NX PX, a unique database key or a Durable Object).
Pick maxNumber for your audience: about 20,000 Web Crypto hashes per second were measured in Node 22, so the default 50,000 averages about 1.3 s; run solveChallenge in a Web Worker.
Pass clientIp only from a header your own proxy sets; never trust a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For.
limitations: Does not render captcha widgets or ship browser UI; add each provider's own script and widget, and call solveChallenge from your form code.

Provider behavior is tested with a fake fetch that follows the documented siteverify fields; no live Turnstile, hCaptcha or reCAPTCHA call was made, and providers can change error codes (unknown codes map to provider-error).
Proof of work raises the cost of bulk submissions but does not stop a determined bot with real compute; solve time varies widely by device and browser and was measured only in Node 22.
MemoryReplayStore lives in one process and is lost on restart; no SQL or Redis store is included.
The honeypot token is not single-use and the minimum fill time only stops naive scripts.
No rate limiting or account-level abuse detection; add rate limits (see the rate-limit module) on the same routes.
Production secret custody, provider configuration, accessibility of the chosen challenge and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: any failed check → 403 bot-check-failed (reasons hidden); body over 64 KiB → 413; other types → 415
proof-of-work challenge at GET {prefix}/challenge?form=<formId>; protect() wraps POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE
reCAPTCHA minScore 0.5; captcha max age 5 min; provider outage fails closed unless failOpen
honeypot field 'website'; submit under 3 s after render → too-fast

behaviors: Turnstile, hCaptcha and reCAPTCHA post form-encoded secret, response and remoteip to their documented siteverify URLs; only Turnstile gets idempotency_key
a wrong or missing hostname, a stale or future challenge_ts and an unparseable timestamp are refused for each provider
provider error codes map to stable reasons and unknown codes become provider-error
an action mismatch is refused for Turnstile and reCAPTCHA, and hCaptcha rejects expectedAction at configuration
a reCAPTCHA v3 score below minScore is refused; v2 replies without a score pass
network errors, non-2xx and unparseable replies give unavailable and fail closed by default; failOpen passes with failedOpen true
the secret never appears in results or thrown configuration errors
a proof-of-work challenge is issued, solved by solveChallenge and verified once; a replay, including 10 concurrent replays, succeeds exactly once
a tampered signature, another key, another form, a changed salt, a wrong number, malformed or missing solutions and expired challenges are refused without consuming the challenge
a filled honeypot, a too-fast submission, a token for another form, a forged or expired token are refused
the combined guard runs honeypot, proof of work and captcha in order and makes no siteverify call after a local failure

protect() returns the same 403 bot-check-failed for every failed check, passes urlencoded, multipart and JSON bodies to the handler intact, and returns 413, 400 or 415 for oversized, invalid or unsupported bodies
the challenge route issues no-store challenges only for configured forms and GET

changes: First release: captcha verification for Turnstile, hCaptcha and reCAPTCHA, proof-of-work challenge and solver, honeypot, combined guard, in-memory replay store and Fetch adapters.
